Date: 2026-07-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Question on cross-region per-token discounts and commit tiers

Hi Logan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran some rough numbers and want to understand how Redwood's usage-based discounts and commit tiers apply when our traffic spans US, EU and APAC. Two quick points that aren't clear from the doc: 

1) If a request originates in APAC but is served from a US model instance (due to capacity), which regional price applies?
2) Can we pool usage across regions under a single commit tier (e.g. 1B tokens/month) and get a blended per-token rate, or do commits have to be region-separated?

I've attached our month-by-month token profile (volume_profile.csv) to show expected splits.

Would appreciate a written example showing how billing would look under a blended bucket vs separate regional buckets. Also looping in our procurement contact (Danielle) on CC.

Best,
Hira
Head of Platform
Aurora Apps

Attachment: volume_profile.csv (csv)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Hira Patel <hira@auroraapps.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T12:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Question on cross-region per-token discounts and commit tiers

Hi Hira —

Thanks for the profile — very helpful. Short answers up front: we support both approaches, but the economics and contract language differ. 

- Model execution region: billing defaults to the region where the model executes (i.e., where the token is generated), not the request origin.
- Commit pooling: we can create a single multi-region commit that provides a blended per-token unit price (recommended for predictable global usage), or we can carve region-specific commits if you need separate budgeting or EU-specific invoicing.

I sketched a short draft that contrasts the two approaches (regional-pricing-draft.pdf). Would you have 30 minutes tomorrow to walk through preferred constraints (billing entity, data residency of invoices, and any legal/regulatory constraints for EU)? If yes I can also include our finance lead and AE to speed approvals.

Cheers,
Logan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: regional-pricing-draft.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Internal: Aurora Apps — proposed commit/discounts after discovery

Team — quick summary and ask from today's call with Aurora Apps (Hira + Danielle):

Call highlights:
- Aurora expects ~600M tokens/mo in steady state with seasonal peaks to ~1.2B; split today is ~55% US, 30% EU, 15% APAC (see attached profile).
- They want predictable unit economics globally and prefer a single P&L view for the App team (one invoice) but legal/procurement may want EU-specific language.
- Procurement (Danielle) asked if we can: 1) provide a blended per-token rate under a multi-region commit, and 2) include a clause that ensures EU invoices and data residency notes when requested.

Proposed commercial approach (draft):
- 12-month committed tier: 1B tokens/month total (multi-region pool) => blended per-token price: $0.00035/token.
- Overage pricing: $0.00050/token (per-token) for usage above commit.
- Regional uplift: when >40% of monthly tokens execute in a single non-US region, apply a +5% uplift to blended rate to cover higher APAC/EU infra costs (waived for first quarter post-signing).
- Separate EU invoicing option: create an EU invoice/legal annex for tax purposes while keeping a single usage pool in accounting.

Questions for finance/legal: is the regional uplift approach doable operationally? If not, we can instead offer a two-bucket commit (US bucket + EU/APAC bucket) with different unit prices.

Attachments: proposed_commit_table.xlsx, call_notes_aurora.txt

Next steps: please reply with redlines/cost guidance so I can package a formal proposal by end of week.

Thanks,
Logan

Thanks Logan — a few finance notes after reviewing the proposed table: 

1) Blended commit: doable but needs an internal mapping to execution region on our side so we can tag tokens for tax/regulatory reporting. We'll need Aurora to sign an annex confirming the pooled model so revenue recognition is clear.

2) Regional uplift: operationally possible but we should cap the uplift at 3% instead of 5% to avoid sticker shock and keep negotiations simple. Alternatively, offer a first-90-day waiver as you suggested.

3) EU invoicing: if they require a separate EU entity invoice, we can support it but need to confirm legal name and VAT ID up front. That will require additional bookkeeping and a short setup fee (one-time, $1,500).

I can model the two variants (single pooled commit with 3% uplift cap + 90-day waiver) and (two-bucket commit) and return the P&L impact by EOD Thursday.

-Monica

Subject: Aurora — formal blended commit proposal and next steps

Hira / Danielle —

Great to speak earlier this week. Based on our call + internal pricing review, please find a formal proposal attached (Aurora_discount_proposal_20260715.pdf). Summary below of the commercial offer and next steps.

Proposal summary:
- Term: 12 months, auto-renew with 60-day notice.
- Commit: 1,000,000,000 tokens/month pooled across US/EU/APAC.
- Blended unit price (pooled): $0.000345/token (applies to tokens executed in any region).
- Regional uplift: capped at +3% applied only if a region exceeds 50% of monthly executed tokens; 90-day waiver from start date.
- Overage rate: $0.00049/token.
- EU invoicing: available as an annex (one-time setup fee $1,500). We will need legal name + VAT ID for the EU invoice.
- Service credits: SLA 99.9% monthly uptime for hosted API; credits scale by downtime minutes (standard T&Cs attached).

Operational notes:
- Billing/usage tagging: Redwood will tag executed tokens by region so reports match invoices.
- Data residency: billing records can be delivered to a EU entity if requested; model execution location will remain near runtime unless pinned by policy (pinning can be added to the contract but may affect latency/cost).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether you prefer pooled billing or two-bucket commits (response by 2026-07-22 keeps pricing intact).
2) If EU invoicing is required, send legal name + VAT ID.
3) If agreed, we will send a DocuSign with the commercial term and EU annex for signature.

Attachments: Aurora_discount_proposal_20260715.pdf (pdf)

Thanks and happy to hop on follow-up call if helpful.

Best,
